en gås.explanation: "En gås" means "a goose", a big bird with a long neck that flies in groups. The meat is also eaten: "gåsesteg" (roast goose).

sentence.da: En **gås** er en stor fugl og bor ved vandet.
sentence.en: A goose is a big bird and lives by the water.

en gåtur.explanation: "En gåtur" means "a walk". It is built from gå (walk) and tur (trip). You say "at gå en tur" or "at tage på gåtur", both meaning "to go for a walk".

sentence.da: Vi tager på **gåtur** i skoven.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in the forest.

en gæld.explanation: "En gæld" means "a debt", money you owe to a person or a bank. It is mostly used without "en": "Hun har ingen gæld" (She has no debt).

sentence.da: Efter huskøbet har de **gæld** til banken.
sentence.en: After buying the house, they have debt to the bank.

en gæst.explanation: "En gæst" means "a guest", for visitors in your home and also for hotel guests: "Vi får gæster" (We are having guests).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad til vores **gæst**.
sentence.en: We cook for our guest.

en gætteleg.explanation: "En gætteleg" means "a guessing game". It is built from at gætte (to guess) and leg (game). "Leg" also gives "at lege" (to play).

sentence.da: I en **gætteleg** skal du gætte svaret.
sentence.en: In a guessing game, you have to guess the answer.

et gab.explanation: "Et gab" means "a yawn", the wide open mouth you make when you are tired or bored. The same word also names the wide open mouth of a big animal, such as a lion's.

sentence.da: Han skjuler et **gab** bag hånden, fordi mødet er så langt.
sentence.en: He hides a yawn behind his hand because the meeting is so long.

et gadekryds.explanation: "Et gadekryds" means "an intersection", where two streets cross. It is built from en gade (a street) and et kryds (a cross). "Kryds" also means a cross mark: "Sæt et kryds her" (Put a cross here).

sentence.da: Drej til højre ved næste **gadekryds**.
sentence.en: Turn right at the next intersection.

et galleri.explanation: "Et galleri" means "a gallery", a place that shows art, often for sale.

sentence.da: Vi ser på kunst i et lille **galleri**.
sentence.en: We look at art in a small gallery.

et gardin.explanation: "Et gardin" means "a curtain", hung at a window. To close it, say "at trække for" (to draw): "Hun trækker gardinerne for" (She closes the curtains).

sentence.da: Et **gardin** hænger foran vinduet og holder lyset ude.
sentence.en: A curtain hangs in front of the window and keeps the light out.

et gavekort.explanation: "Et gavekort" means "a gift card", a card with money on it that you give as a present. It is made of en gave (a gift) and et kort (a card).

sentence.da: Med et **gavekort** kan man købe ting.
sentence.en: With a gift card you can buy things.

et gear.explanation: "Et gear" means "a gear", one of the settings on a car or a bike that you shift between to go faster or climb hills.

sentence.da: Jeg skifter **gear**, når vejen går opad.
sentence.en: I shift gears when the road goes uphill.

et gebyr.explanation: "Et gebyr" means "a fee", an amount you pay to a bank, an authority or a company for a service, or for being late: "et rykkergebyr" (a reminder fee).

sentence.da: Banken tager et **gebyr** på halvtreds kroner for hver overførsel.
sentence.en: The bank charges a fee of fifty kroner for each transfer.

et gen.explanation: "Et gen" means "a gene", a tiny unit inside the body that carries instructions passed from parents to children, for example for eye color. Danes also say "Det ligger i generne" (It runs in the family), literally "It lies in the genes".

sentence.da: Hvert **gen** bærer instruktioner om, hvordan kroppen skal bygges.
sentence.en: Each gene carries instructions about how the body is built.

et geni.explanation: "Et geni" means "a genius", a person with a brilliant mind. To name the subject a person is brilliant at, use "i" (in) or "til" (at): "Hun er et geni i matematik" (She is a genius at math).

sentence.da: Min bror er et **geni** til matematik.
sentence.en: My brother is a genius at math.

et gennembrud.explanation: "Et gennembrud" means "a breakthrough", a big step forward that comes after a long period of effort, in science, sport or a career. For an artist, it is the moment they become well known: "Hendes gennembrud kom i 2010" (Her breakthrough came in 2010).

sentence.da: Efter mange års arbejde fik forskerne endelig et **gennembrud**.
sentence.en: After many years of work, the researchers finally got a breakthrough.

et gennemsnit.explanation: "Et gennemsnit" means "an average", the number you get by adding a list of numbers and dividing by how many there are. Danes also use it for what is typical: "over gennemsnittet" (above average).

sentence.da: Jeg sover syv timer i **gennemsnit**.
sentence.en: I sleep seven hours on average.

et gerningssted.explanation: "Et gerningssted" means "a crime scene", the place where a crime happened. The police close it off with tape and search it carefully, so nobody disturbs the evidence.

sentence.da: Det sted, hvor en forbrydelse er sket, kaldes et **gerningssted**.
sentence.en: The place where a crime has happened is called a crime scene.

et gevir.explanation: "Et gevir" means "a set of antlers", the branched bony growth on the head of a stag.

sentence.da: Hjorten har et stort **gevir** med mange spidser.
sentence.en: The deer has a large set of antlers with many points.

et gevær.explanation: "Et gevær" means "a rifle", a long gun that you hold against your shoulder when you fire it, used for hunting and by soldiers. A small gun held in one hand is "en pistol" (a pistol).

sentence.da: Jægeren sigter omhyggeligt, før han skyder med sit **gevær**.
sentence.en: The hunter aims carefully before he shoots with his rifle.

et gidsel.explanation: "Et gidsel" means "a hostage", a person who is held by someone who wants something in return. You say "at tage nogen som gidsel" (to take someone hostage).

sentence.da: Bankrøveren holder et **gidsel**, og politiet forhandler med ham.
sentence.en: The bank robber is holding a hostage, and the police are negotiating with him.

et glas.explanation: "Et glas" means "a glass", both the material and a drinking glass. Danish has no word for "of" here: "et glas vand" (a glass of water) and "et glas vin" (a glass of wine).

sentence.da: Man drikker vand af et **glas**.
sentence.en: You drink water from a glass.

et glimt.explanation: "Et glimt" means "a glimpse" and "a gleam": a very short sight of something, or a brief flash of light. A playful look in someone's eye is "et glimt i øjet" (a twinkle in the eye).

sentence.da: Hun fik et **glimt** af solen mellem skyerne.
sentence.en: She got a glimpse of the sun between the clouds.

et gram.explanation: "Et gram" means "a gram", a unit of weight used for small amounts, such as flour or spices.

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge to hundrede **gram** mel.
sentence.en: I need two hundred grams of flour.

et grin.explanation: "Et grin" means "a laugh" or "a grin". For a smile, say "et smil" (a smile).

sentence.da: Vi fik et godt **grin** sammen i går.
sentence.en: We had a good laugh together yesterday.

et grundlag.explanation: "Et grundlag" means "a basis", the base that something rests on, such as a decision, a law or an argument. A common phrase is "et solidt grundlag" (a solid basis).

sentence.da: Aftalen blev det **grundlag**, som resten af planen byggede på.
sentence.en: The agreement became the basis that the rest of the plan was built on.

et grundstof.explanation: "Et grundstof" means "a chemical element", a pure material that chemistry cannot break down into anything simpler, such as "ilt" (oxygen) or "jern" (iron). All other materials are made by combining these.

sentence.da: Guld er et **grundstof**, som ikke kan deles i noget enklere.
sentence.en: Gold is an element that cannot be split into anything simpler.

et gudbarn.explanation: "Et gudbarn" means "a godchild", a child you are a godparent to.

sentence.da: Mit **gudbarn** fylder fem år i dag.
sentence.en: My godchild turns five today.

et guldbryllup.explanation: "Et guldbryllup" means "a golden wedding anniversary", the celebration of 50 years of marriage. The word is only for the anniversary party: the day of the wedding itself is "et bryllup" (a wedding).

sentence.da: Mine bedsteforældre har været gift i halvtreds år og holder **guldbryllup**.
sentence.en: My grandparents have been married for fifty years and are celebrating their golden wedding.

et gulv.explanation: "Et gulv" means "a floor", the surface you walk on in a room. For a level of a building, use "en etage" (a story): "anden etage" (second floor).

sentence.da: Et **gulv** er lavet af træ eller sten.
sentence.en: A floor is made of wood or stone.

et gulvtæppe.explanation: "Et gulvtæppe" means "a carpet", a large covering that lies over the floor of a room. A small one you can move around is "et tæppe" (a rug).

sentence.da: Vi har et blødt **gulvtæppe** i stuen.
sentence.en: We have a soft carpet in the living room.

et gymnasium.explanation: "Et gymnasium" means "a high school", the three years, at about age 16 to 19, that prepare you for university. It is not a gym: a sports hall is "en idrætshal" (a sports hall).

sentence.da: Efter folkeskolen går mange unge på et **gymnasium**.
sentence.en: After primary school, many young people go to a gymnasium.

et gys.explanation: "Et gys" means "a shudder", a quick shiver through the body, caused by cold, fear or disgust. "Det gav mig et gys" (It gave me a shudder) says that something scared or disgusted you.

sentence.da: Et **gys** løb ned ad ryggen på mig, da døren gik op.
sentence.en: A shudder ran down my back when the door opened.

et gæsteværelse.explanation: "Et gæsteværelse" means "a guest room", the room in your home for people who sleep over. It is built from gæst (guest) and værelse (room).

sentence.da: Du kan sove i vores **gæsteværelse**.
sentence.en: You can sleep in our guest room.

et gøremål.explanation: "Et gøremål" means "a chore", a small thing you need to get done, often at home or on a to-do list. It is mostly used in the plural: "dagens gøremål" (today's chores).

sentence.da: Jeg har mange **gøremål** i dag, blandt andet at handle og vaske tøj.
sentence.en: I have many chores today, including shopping and washing clothes.

gal.explanation: "Gal" means "crazy", for a person or idea that is mad or foolish. The form "galt" is used for "wrong": "Noget gik galt" (Something went wrong).

sentence.da: Er du helt **gal**? Det er alt for farligt!
sentence.en: Are you completely crazy? That is far too dangerous!

galskab.explanation: "En galskab" means "madness" in the sense of a wild, reckless act or idea. It is usually about foolish behavior rather than a medical condition.

sentence.da: Det er rent **galskab** at sejle i den storm.
sentence.en: It is pure madness to sail in that storm.

galt.explanation: "Galt" means "wrong": "Jeg gjorde noget galt" (I did something wrong). With an en-word, use "gal" instead, which also means "crazy": "en gal idé" (a crazy idea).

sentence.da: Noget er **galt** med min computer.
sentence.en: Something is wrong with my computer.

gammel.explanation: "Gammel" means "old", for things ("en gammel bil", an old car) and for a person's age. To ask age, you say "Hvor gammel er du?" (How old are you?) and answer "Jeg er tredive år gammel" (I am thirty years old).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er 90 år og meget **gammel**.
sentence.en: My grandfather is 90 and very old.

gammeldags.explanation: "Gammeldags" means "old-fashioned". You write it the same before en-words and et-words: "en gammeldags bil" (an old-fashioned car), "et gammeldags hus" (an old-fashioned house). The opposite is "moderne" (modern).

sentence.da: Min mormor har et **gammeldags** køkken.
sentence.en: My grandmother has an old-fashioned kitchen.

gang.explanation: "Gang" means "a time" in the sense of an occasion: "en gang" means "once", "to gange" means "twice", and "Hvor mange gange?" means "How many times?". It can also mean a hallway in a house. For time as hours and minutes, use "tid": "Jeg har ikke tid" (I do not have time).

sentence.da: Jeg har været i Paris en **gang**.
sentence.en: I have been to Paris once.

ganske.explanation: "Ganske" means "quite" or "fairly". It is weaker than "meget" (very), so "ganske kold" (quite cold) is less cold than "meget kold" (very cold).

sentence.da: Maden var **ganske** god, men lidt dyr.
sentence.en: The food was quite good, but a little expensive.

ganske vist.explanation: "Ganske vist" means "admittedly" and admits a point first, so a sentence with "men" (but) usually follows: "Det er ganske vist dyrt, men det er godt" (It is admittedly expensive, but it is good).

forms.da: Hun kom ganske vist for sent

sentence.da: Bilen er **ganske vist** gammel, men den kører fint.
sentence.en: The car is admittedly old, but it runs fine.

garanteret.explanation: "Garanteret" means "guaranteed". In everyday speech you also say it when you are almost certain, even without proof, and it is stronger than "sikkert" (probably): "Han kommer garanteret for sent" (He is sure to be late).

sentence.da: Når du øver dig hver dag, bliver du **garanteret** bedre.
sentence.en: When you practice every day, you will definitely get better.

gavepapir.explanation: "Gavepapir" means "wrapping paper", the paper you wrap presents in. It is built from gave (present) and papir (paper). To count it, say "en rulle gavepapir" (a roll of wrapping paper).

sentence.da: Jeg pakker gaven ind i rødt **gavepapir**.
sentence.en: I wrap the gift in red wrapping paper.

gavmild.explanation: "Gavmild" means "generous" and describes a person who gives freely of money, time or things.

sentence.da: Han er **gavmild** og betaler ofte for alle sine venner.
sentence.en: He is generous and often pays for all his friends.

gavmildhed.explanation: "En gavmildhed" means "generosity", a readiness to give more than is expected. It comes from gavmild (generous), which is made of gave (gifts) and mild (gentle).

sentence.da: Det var et tegn på **gavmildhed**, at han betalte for alle.
sentence.en: It was a sign of generosity that he paid for everyone.

gavn.explanation: "Gavn" means "benefit" or "use", the good that something does for someone. It is mostly used after "til" (to): "til gavn for børn" (for the benefit of children).

forms.en: to get use out of something

sentence.da: Motion er til stor **gavn** for hjertet.
sentence.en: Exercise is of great benefit to the heart.

genbrug.explanation: "Genbrug" means "recycling", using things again instead of discarding them. It covers both turning old material into something new and reusing an item as it is.

sentence.da: Gamle flasker kan blive til nye ting ved **genbrug**.
sentence.en: Old bottles can become new things through recycling.

generelt.explanation: "Generelt" means "generally" and says what is true overall, though not in every case. One specific day can be different: "Generelt er bussen til tiden, men i dag var den sen" (Generally the bus is on time, but today it was late).

sentence.da: **Generelt** er det varmt i juli, men ikke altid.
sentence.en: Generally it is warm in July, but not always.

genert.explanation: "Genert" means "shy", nervous around other people. "Over for" (towards) says who you are shy around: "Han er genert over for fremmede" (He is shy around strangers).

sentence.da: Jeg er lidt **genert**, når jeg møder nye folk.
sentence.en: I am a bit shy when I meet new people.

generøs.explanation: "Generøs" means "generous" and describes someone who gives freely. "Med" (with) says what is given: "Hun er generøs med sin tid" (She is generous with her time). The opposite is "nærig" (stingy).

sentence.da: Han er **generøs** og giver gerne penge væk.
sentence.en: He is generous and gladly gives money away.

generøsitet.explanation: "En generøsitet" means "generosity", being willing to give money, time or help freely. It is often used to thank someone: "Vi takker for din generøsitet" (We thank you for your generosity).

sentence.da: Det er **generøsitet**, når man giver uden at forvente noget.
sentence.en: It is generosity when you give without expecting anything.

genetik.explanation: "Genetik" means "genetics", the science of how traits are passed from parents to children. It is also used for the traits themselves: "Det ligger i genetikken" (It is in the genes).

sentence.da: Inden for **genetik** studerer man, hvad børn arver fra deres forældre.
sentence.en: In genetics, you study what children inherit from their parents.

genetisk.explanation: "Genetisk" means "genetic", describing something that comes from the DNA passed on by parents. It comes from "genetik" (genetics).

sentence.da: Sygdommen er **genetisk** og går i arv i familien.
sentence.en: The disease is genetic and runs in the family.

genial.explanation: "Genial" means "brilliant", extremely clever. You can use it for an idea or for a person: "Hun er genial" (She is brilliant).

sentence.da: Det er en **genial** idé, og den virker.
sentence.en: It is a brilliant idea, and it works.

gennem.explanation: "Gennem" means "through". With time, it means "throughout": "Jeg har boet her gennem mange år" (I have lived here for many years).

sentence.da: Vi går **gennem** parken hjem.
sentence.en: We walk home through the park.

gennemført.explanation: "Gennemført" means "polished", worked out from start to end so that no part feels out of place. It comes from at gennemføre (to carry out).

sentence.da: Koncerten var en **gennemført** oplevelse fra start til slut.
sentence.en: The concert was a polished experience from start to finish.

gennemsigtig.explanation: "Gennemsigtig" means "transparent", so light passes through and you can see what is behind. It is built from gennem (through) and sigt (sight). It also describes things that are easy to follow and hide nothing: "en gennemsigtig proces" (a transparent process).

sentence.da: Ruden er **gennemsigtig**, og man kan se ud igennem den.
sentence.en: The window is transparent, and you can see out through it.

gennemsnitlig.explanation: "Gennemsnitlig" means "average", based on the average of many values. For "ordinary, nothing special", Danes use "almindelig" (ordinary) instead.

sentence.da: Det er en **gennemsnitlig** pris, ikke den billigste og ikke den dyreste.
sentence.en: It is an average price, not the cheapest and not the most expensive.

genoptræning.explanation: "Genoptræning" means "rehabilitation", exercise and therapy that help you regain strength and movement after an injury or an operation. The "gen-" at the start means "again", as in "at gentage" (to repeat).

sentence.da: Efter operationen går jeg til **genoptræning** i tre måneder.
sentence.en: After the surgery, I go to rehabilitation for three months.

gensidighed.explanation: "Gensidighed" means "mutuality", when both sides give and get in the same way, such as respect or help going in both directions. It comes from gensidig (mutual).

sentence.da: I et godt forhold skal der være **gensidighed**.
sentence.en: In a good relationship, there must be mutuality.

geografi.explanation: "Geografi" means "geography", the study of countries and landscapes at school.

sentence.da: Vi lærer om lande og floder i **geografi**.
sentence.en: We learn about countries and rivers in geography.

gerne.explanation: "Gerne" means "gladly". When you ask for something, "gerne" makes it polite: "Jeg vil have en øl" (I want a beer) sounds blunt, while "Jeg vil gerne have en øl" (I would like a beer) is polite. When you offer help, "gerne" says you are glad to do it: "Jeg hjælper dig gerne" (I am glad to help you).

forms.en: I am happy to do that.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **gerne** have en kop te.
sentence.en: I would like a cup of tea.

gerrig.explanation: "Gerrig" means "stingy", very unwilling to spend or share, even when there is plenty. It is clearly negative: someone careful with money in a good way is "sparsommelig" (thrifty).

sentence.da: Han er så **gerrig**, at han aldrig giver drikkepenge.
sentence.en: He is so stingy that he never gives tips.

gerrighed.explanation: "En gerrighed" means "stinginess", the trait of hating to spend money or share. It is clearly negative, unlike "sparsommelighed" (thrift), which means being careful with money in a good way.

sentence.da: Hans **gerrighed** betød, at familien aldrig fik gaver.
sentence.en: His stinginess meant that the family never got gifts.

gift.explanation: "Gift" means "married". To name the partner, add "med" (with) after "gift": "gift med Peter" (married to Peter). The same spelling is also the word for poison, and you can tell which one it is from the context of the sentence.

sentence.da: Jeg er **gift** med Anna.
sentence.en: I am married to Anna.

gin.explanation: "Gin" means "gin", a clear strong drink with a juniper taste. Without "en" it means the drink itself: "Jeg kan ikke lide gin" (I do not like gin). With "en" it means one serving: "Hun drikker en gin" (She is drinking a gin).

sentence.da: Hun bestiller en **gin** og tonic i baren.
sentence.en: She orders a gin and tonic at the bar.

glad.explanation: "Glad" means "happy", the everyday word for feeling pleased or cheerful. To name the thing that makes you happy, add "for" (about) after "glad": "Jeg er glad for gaven" (I am happy about the gift).

sentence.da: Drengen smiler og er så **glad**.
sentence.en: The boy smiles and is so happy.

glad for.explanation: "Glad for" means "fond of" or "happy with" something or someone. It is milder than "elske" (to love): "Jeg er glad for dig" (I am fond of you).

forms.da: Hun er glad for sin bil.
forms.en: She is happy with her car.

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **glad for** min lejlighed.
sentence.en: I am very happy with my apartment.

glat.explanation: "Glat" means "smooth", with no bumps or roughness. It also means "slippery", for things like ice or a wet road.

sentence.da: Pas på, gulvet er **glat**.
sentence.en: Be careful, the floor is slippery.

sentence.da: Du har lavet et **glimrende** stykke arbejde.
sentence.en: You have done an excellent piece of work.

global.explanation: "Global" means "global", covering the whole Earth, not just one country. It is spelled like the English word.

sentence.da: Klimaet er en **global** udfordring, ikke kun en dansk.
sentence.en: The climate is a global challenge, not only a Danish one.

global opvarmning.explanation: "Global opvarmning" means "global warming", the rise in the Earth's average temperature over many years. "Opvarmning" comes from "at varme op" (to warm up), where "op" means "up".

sentence.da: **Global opvarmning** får isen ved polerne til at smelte.
sentence.en: Global warming makes the ice at the poles melt.

gluten.explanation: "Gluten" means "gluten", the protein in many types of grain. To say without it, add "-fri" (free): "glutenfri" (gluten-free).

sentence.da: Der er **gluten** i hvedebrød.
sentence.en: There is gluten in wheat bread.

glutenfri.explanation: "Glutenfri" means "gluten-free", made without gluten. It is built from gluten and fri (free). "Fri" works the same in many words: "alkoholfri" (alcohol-free).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser kun **glutenfri** pasta.
sentence.en: I only eat gluten-free pasta.

glæde.explanation: "Glæde" means "joy". "At glæde sig" means to look forward to something: "Jeg glæder mig til ferien" (I am looking forward to the vacation).

sentence.da: Hendes ansigt lyste af **glæde**.
sentence.en: Her face lit up with joy.

glædelig jul.explanation: "Glædelig jul" means "merry Christmas". "Glædelig" means "merry" and "jul" means "Christmas". A reply is "i lige måde" (same to you), and you can add "og godt nytår" (and happy New Year).

forms.en: Merry Christmas and happy New Year.

sentence.da: Vi har gaver og et juletræ. **Glædelig jul**!
sentence.en: We have presents and a Christmas tree. Merry Christmas!

glødende.explanation: "Glødende" means "glowing", about something so hot that it shines, like embers or hot metal. It also means "passionate": "en glødende tilhænger" (a passionate supporter). It comes from "at gløde" (to glow).

sentence.da: Smeden tog det **glødende** jern ud af ilden.
sentence.en: The blacksmith took the glowing iron out of the fire.

gløgg.explanation: "Gløgg" means "mulled wine", a hot, spiced red wine drunk in winter, especially in December. It is often served with raisins and almonds.

forms.en: mulled wine and Danish pancake balls

sentence.da: I december drikker mange varm **gløgg** for at holde varmen.
sentence.en: In December, many people drink hot mulled wine to keep warm.

gnaven.explanation: "Gnaven" means "grumpy", in a bad mood and snapping at people over small things. You can say it about a tone of voice too: "en gnaven stemme" (a grumpy voice).

sentence.da: Min bror er altid **gnaven**, når han er sulten.
sentence.en: My brother is always grumpy when he is hungry.

god.explanation: "God" means "good", and it appears in greetings like "god morgen" (good morning) and "godt nytår" (happy New Year). To say something goes well, use "godt": "Det går godt" (It is going well).

sentence.da: Han hjælper altid. Han er en **god** ven.
sentence.en: He always helps. He is a good friend.

god appetit.explanation: "God appetit" means "enjoy your meal", like bon appétit, and is said just before eating. Danes also say "velbekomme" (enjoy / you are welcome), often when the food is served or after the meal. A reply is "i lige måde" (same to you) or "tak" (thanks).

sentence.da: Maden er klar. **God appetit**!
sentence.en: The food is ready. Enjoy your meal!

god bedring.explanation: "God bedring" means "get well soon" and is said to someone who is sick or hurt. "Bedring" means "improvement", so you are wishing them a good recovery.

forms.en: Get well soon with your cold.

sentence.da: Du er syg? **God bedring**!
sentence.en: Are you sick? Get well soon!

god fornøjelse.explanation: "God fornøjelse" means "enjoy", said to someone who is about to see or do something fun. Do not use it for a meal; say "god appetit" (enjoy your meal) instead.

sentence.da: Vi skal i teatret. **God fornøjelse**!
sentence.en: We are going to the theater. Enjoy!

god påske.explanation: "God påske" means "happy Easter" and is said before and during the Easter holiday. A reply is "i lige måde" (same to you).

sentence.da: Vi ses efter ferien. **God påske**!
sentence.en: See you after the holiday. Happy Easter!

god til.explanation: "God til" means "good at" something. To name a subject, add "til" (to) and the subject: "god til matematik" (good at math). To name an activity, add "til at" before the action word: "god til at synge" (good at singing).

forms.da: Jeg er god til at lave mad.
Han er ikke god til sport.
forms.en: He is not good at sports.

sentence.da: Han er **god til** at spille fodbold.
sentence.en: He is good at playing soccer.

god tur.explanation: "God tur" means "have a good trip" and is said to anyone setting off, whether by car, train, bike or plane. For a longer journey, you can say "god rejse" (have a good journey). A reply is "tak" (thanks).

forms.en: Have a good trip to Copenhagen.

sentence.da: Vi tager af sted nu. — **God tur**!
sentence.en: We are leaving now. — Have a good trip!

god weekend.explanation: "God weekend" means "have a good weekend". It is said when parting before the weekend. A reply is "i lige måde" (same to you). On Monday, people ask "Havde du en god weekend?" (Did you have a good weekend?).

forms.en: Have a good weekend, all of you.

sentence.da: Vi ses på mandag. **God weekend**!
sentence.en: See you on Monday. Have a good weekend!

godaften.explanation: "Godaften" means "good evening". You say it when you meet someone in the evening. Do not use it when you go to bed; then you say "godnat" (good night).

sentence.da: **Godaften**, Peter! Hvordan har du det?
sentence.en: Good evening, Peter! How are you?

goddag.explanation: "Goddag" means "good day", a polite way to say hello at any time of day. With friends, say "hej" (hi) instead. You can answer "goddag" with "goddag".

sentence.da: **Goddag**, jeg hedder Peter.
sentence.en: Hello, my name is Peter.

godhed.explanation: "En godhed" means "goodness", being warm and caring toward others.

sentence.da: Alle kender hende for hendes **godhed** mod dyr.
sentence.en: Everyone knows her for her goodness toward animals.

godmorgen.explanation: "Godmorgen" means "good morning", said until late morning. For later in the day, you switch to "goddag" (good day).

sentence.da: **Godmorgen**! Har du sovet godt?
sentence.en: Good morning! Did you sleep well?

godnat.explanation: "Godnat" means "good night" and is said when you or someone else is going to bed, or when you part late in the evening. It is not a greeting for meeting someone: for that use "godaften" (good evening).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og går i seng. **Godnat**!
sentence.en: I am tired and going to bed. Good night!

godt nytår.explanation: "Godt nytår" means "happy New Year". It uses "godt" (good) because "nytår" (New Year) is an et-word, so it is not "god nytår". A reply is "i lige måde" (same to you).

forms.en: Happy New Year to you all.

sentence.da: Det er midnat. **Godt nytår**!
sentence.en: It is midnight. Happy New Year!

golf.explanation: "Golf" means "golf", the sport where you hit a small ball into holes with clubs.

sentence.da: Jeg spiller **golf** på en grøn bane.
sentence.en: I play golf on a green course.

grader.explanation: "Grader" means "degrees", used for temperature. For below zero, Danes say "minus": "Det er minus to grader" (It is minus two degrees).

sentence.da: Der er kun fem **grader** udenfor.
sentence.en: It is only five degrees outside.

gradvist.explanation: "Gradvist" means "gradually", changing a little at a time instead of all at once. To describe a thing, use "gradvis" (gradual): "en gradvis ændring" (a gradual change).

sentence.da: Isen smelter ikke på én dag, men **gradvist** over flere uger.
sentence.en: The ice does not melt in one day, but gradually over several weeks.

gratis.explanation: "Gratis" means "free", as in costing no money. Do not mix it up with "fri", which means off from work or school: "Jeg har fri i dag" (I have the day off today).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke betale. Det er **gratis**.
sentence.en: You do not have to pay. It is free.

grillkul.explanation: "Grillkul" means "charcoal", the fuel for a barbecue. It is built from grill (barbecue) and kul (coal).

sentence.da: Vi lægger **grillkul** i grillen og tænder det.
sentence.en: We put charcoal in the grill and light it.

grim.explanation: "Grim" means "ugly" and can describe anyone or anything that looks bad, such as a person or a building. It can also mean unpleasant: "grimt vejr" (nasty weather) and "et grimt ord" (a nasty word). Saying "Du er grim" (You are ugly) to a person is very rude.

sentence.da: Bygningen er **grim** og ikke smuk.
sentence.en: The building is ugly and not beautiful.
